_readme: Curated, human-reviewed facts for the 2027 application cycle.
roll-cycle.mjs reads this file and applies it on top of the automatic
one-year roll-forward. Anything NOT listed here is rolled forward
automatically and flagged verification:'projected' so the UI can say
'expected date — confirm on the official site'.
To prepare next year's update: copy this file to cycle-2028-updates.json,
replace the contents, and run `npm run roll-cycle -- --cycle 2028`.

discontinued.reason: Google has not run a CSSI cohort in recent years and no application cycle has been announced. The curriculum site remains online as a self-study resource, but there is no cohort to apply to.
discontinued.successor: Google's current high-school CS outreach runs through Code Next and the Build Your Future site.

uncertain.reason: The Ithaca TASS 2026 seminar closed on July 3, 2026 — roughly three weeks early — after residential staff departures. Telluride Association has not yet announced whether TASS will run in 2027.

verified.note: Applications for RSI 2027 open in October 2026 and close in early-to-mid December 2026 (typically the Wednesday of the second full week). Late applications are never considered.
SSP 2027 applications open in September 2026 and close in February 2027. Open to students graduating high school in 2028.
The SIMR 2027 application and program information document go live December 18, 2026 at 5pm PST. Tentative program dates are June 7 – July 29, 2027.
The Simons application opens in the autumn of the preceding academic year. Start assembling materials — especially your faculty mentor nomination — no later than November 2026.
MITES runs a common application across MITES Summer, MITES Semester and MOSTEC. The deadline has held at February 1 for several cycles; recommendations are due about two weeks later.
Shares the single MITES common application with MITES Summer and MOSTEC.

verified.match: COSMOS — CA Summer School for Math & Science
verified.note: One application covers all four COSMOS campuses (Davis, Irvine, San Diego, Santa Cruz) — you rank your campus and cluster preferences. Applications open in January and close February 8, 2027. Priority goes to California residents.

Two-stage process: self-register for the free online prerequisite course when it opens in early February, complete it, and you are then invited to apply for the summer program by April 15, 2027. No housing is provided — students arrange their own. US students up to 11th grade only.

openings._comment: Application-opening dates that ARE published, for programs whose deadline is not yet announced. Recording these does not promote the projected deadline to verified.
openings.note: The PROMYS 2027 application launches in January 2027; the deadline has not been published yet and the date shown is last cycle's, rolled forward. Six weeks at Boston University, and free for domestic students with family income under $80,000. You can sign up at promys.org to be notified when the application opens.

Mathcamp announces its 2027 dates and location in December 2026, and posts the application and Qualifying Quiz in January 2027. The Quiz is the heart of the application — it is graded on how you reason, not just on final answers, so start it early.

The YYGS application opens in September 2026. Applications that include the need-based financial aid portion must be complete by January 6, 2027; the general deadline shown here is last cycle's, rolled forward. Early Action applicants are either admitted or deferred into the Regular Decision pool.

Applications open in the autumn, typically around October. A paid eight-week summer internship with a local nonprofit plus a week-long leadership summit in Washington, DC. The deadline shown is last cycle's, rolled forward — confirm on the Bank of America site once the cycle opens.

notes._comment: Context only — no date claim. Used where sources disagree or nothing is published yet.
notes.note: Seven weeks of fully funded faculty-mentored research at Texas Tech, with a $750 completion stipend. The 2027 deadline is expected in early-to-mid February but published dates currently disagree — confirm on depts.ttu.edu/clarkscholars before relying on the date shown. Rising seniors and recent graduates who are 17 by the start date.

Stanford has not published the 2027 deadline; the date shown is last cycle's, rolled forward, and recent cycles have closed anywhere from late February to mid-March. Financial-aid documents are generally due in February. Four weeks, mid-July to mid-August, with both online and residential options.

Seven weeks of polymer-science and materials research at Stony Brook. The 2027 deadline is expected around March 1 but is not yet confirmed. Applicants must be 16 by roughly early July and typically need an unweighted 3.8/4.0 (95/100) GPA.

SEES has not published its 2027 deadline; applications have historically opened in October and closed in February. If SEES doesn't work out, NASA's wider OSTEM internship programme lists a Summer 2027 deadline of February 26, 2027 — a separate application, also open to high schoolers.

newPrograms.name: Ross Mathematics Program
newPrograms.desc: One of the oldest and most respected number-theory immersion programs in the world, running since 1957. Students spend six weeks on a single deep problem set exploring the integers from first principles — the motto is 'think deeply of simple things.' No lectures-and-homework rhythm: you build the mathematics yourself with counselor guidance. Alumni populate math faculties worldwide.
newPrograms.note: Applications typically open in early January and close at the end of March. Expect to spend serious time on the entrance problem set — it is the core of the application.

newPrograms.name: Boston University RISE
newPrograms.dates: Six weeks, late June – early August 2027
newPrograms.desc: Research in Science & Engineering places rising seniors in a BU lab for six weeks under a graduate-student or postdoc mentor, working on a genuine research question. Choose the Internship track (lab placement) or the Practicum track (group project in computational neurobiology or similar). Ends with a poster symposium.
newPrograms.note: The internship track is substantially more competitive than the practicum. Financial aid is real but limited — apply early if you need it.

newPrograms.name: Jackson Laboratory Summer Student Program
newPrograms.desc: Ten weeks of independent genetics and genomics research at one of the world's leading mammalian-genetics institutes, on the coast of Maine next to Acadia National Park. Students are paired with a JAX faculty mentor, design their own project, and present at a closing symposium. Housing, meals and travel are covered and students receive a stipend.
newPrograms.note: Extremely competitive — a few dozen places against well over a thousand applicants. Free, paid, and residential, which is a rare combination.

newPrograms.name: NIH Summer Internship Program (SIP)
newPrograms.desc: Paid biomedical research internships in NIH's intramural labs — the largest biomedical research enterprise in the world. High school students work alongside principal investigators on real projects across immunology, neuroscience, cancer biology, bioinformatics and more. Must be 17 by the program start date and a US citizen or permanent resident.
newPrograms.note: Applying is only half the job — you must also email individual investigators whose work interests you. Applicants who contact PIs directly are far more likely to be placed.

newPrograms.name: Rockefeller University Summer Science Research Program
newPrograms.desc: Seven weeks of hands-on laboratory research at a Nobel-laureate-dense biomedical institute on Manhattan's Upper East Side. Students join a working lab, are mentored by a scientist, and present their findings at a final symposium. Includes a stipend. Strongly oriented toward New York-area students.
newPrograms.note: Applications generally open in December and close in early January — one of the earliest deadlines in the cycle. Don't wait for spring.

newPrograms.name: MSK HOPP Summer Student Program
newPrograms.desc: The Human Oncology and Pathogenesis Program places high school students in cancer-research labs at MSK for a full eight-week summer. Students are assigned a mentor, run a project, attend a lecture series on cancer biology, and present a poster at the end. Paid.
newPrograms.note: You must be 18 by the program start date for most lab placements — check the current eligibility rules before investing time in the application.

newPrograms.name: Princeton Summer Journalism Program
newPrograms.dates: Ten-day residency, August 2027, plus a year-long college-admissions component
newPrograms.desc: A free, all-expenses-paid journalism intensive for low-income high school juniors. Students report and publish a real newspaper, meet working journalists from national outlets, and then receive a full year of free college-admissions counselling afterwards. Travel, housing and meals are all covered.
newPrograms.note: Strict income eligibility (household income near or below the federal median). The year-long admissions counselling afterwards is arguably worth more than the ten days themselves.

newPrograms.name: MIT MOSTEC
newPrograms.dates: June 2027 – February 2028 (online, with a campus conference)
newPrograms.desc: MIT Online Science, Technology and Engineering Community — a free six-month online program for rising seniors from underrepresented or underserved backgrounds. Two science-and-engineering courses, a science-writing course, mentoring, and a fully funded trip to MIT for a closing conference. Runs from the summer through the following winter.
newPrograms.note: Shares the single MITES common application with MITES Summer and MITES Semester — one form, three programs, ranked by preference.

newPrograms.name: Perimeter Institute ISSYP
newPrograms.desc: The International Summer School for Young Physicists brings students to Perimeter Institute for two weeks of quantum mechanics, general relativity, cosmology and particle physics taught by working theoretical physicists. Runs both a virtual cohort and a smaller in-person cohort. Tuition, accommodation and meals are free for the in-person school.
newPrograms.note: Open to students worldwide. The virtual edition takes many more students than the in-person one — apply to both if eligible.

newPrograms.name: Iowa Young Writers' Studio
newPrograms.desc: The high school arm of the Iowa Writers' Workshop, the most storied creative-writing program in America. Two weeks of daily workshop in fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, playwriting or TV writing, taught by Iowa MFA writers. Admission is by writing sample.
newPrograms.note: Admission is purely on the strength of the writing sample — grades and test scores are not considered. A shorter online session also runs each summer.

newPrograms.name: Kenyon Review Young Writers Workshop
newPrograms.desc: Two weeks of intensive generative writing run by The Kenyon Review, one of the country's leading literary magazines. Small workshops, twice-daily writing sessions, no grades, no genre requirements. Focused on generating new work rather than polishing a portfolio.
newPrograms.note: Admission is rolling and sessions fill early — applying in January or February is meaningfully better than waiting for spring.

newPrograms.name: Notre Dame Leadership Seminars
newPrograms.desc: A fully funded two-week seminar for about 100 rising seniors, built around discussion-based courses on questions of ethics, justice and human dignity. Tuition, housing and meals are covered by Notre Dame; students pay only travel. Highly selective and academically demanding.
newPrograms.note: One of very few genuinely free humanities-oriented pre-college programs at a major university.

newPrograms.name: UC Santa Cruz Science Internship Program (SIP)
newPrograms.desc: Ten weeks of authentic research on a UCSC team led by a graduate student or postdoc, across astronomy, genomics, engineering, ecology, physics and more. Students contribute to an ongoing project rather than a manufactured exercise, and many go on to co-author posters or papers. Both residential and remote placements.
newPrograms.note: One of the larger authentic-research programs by cohort size, which makes it meaningfully less of a lottery than the tiny lab programs.

newPrograms.name: Naval Academy Summer STEM Program
newPrograms.desc: A one-week residential STEM immersion on the Naval Academy's Annapolis campus — robotics, cyber, naval architecture, propulsion and materials, taught in USNA labs by academy faculty and midshipmen. Separate rising-9th, -10th and -11th grade sessions with age-appropriate curricula.
newPrograms.note: Cheap for what it is, and no service obligation. Attending does not commit you to a military path but does signal genuine interest if you later apply to a service academy.

newPrograms.name: West Point Summer Leaders Experience
newPrograms.host: United States Military Academy at West Point
newPrograms.desc: A one-week look at cadet life for rising seniors seriously considering West Point: academic workshops, military training, physical fitness testing, and living in the barracks. Participation is a documented data point in the West Point admissions file.
newPrograms.note: Effectively part of the West Point admissions funnel. Applications open in January and the cohort fills before the stated deadline.

newPrograms.name: SPARC
newPrograms.host: Summer Program on Applied Rationality and Cognition
newPrograms.desc: A free two-week program in quantitative reasoning, probability, decision theory, game theory and cognitive science for mathematically strong high schoolers. Draws heavily from the olympiad and competition-math community. Instructors come from research, quantitative finance and AI labs.
newPrograms.note: Free including room and board. The application is unusual — expect puzzles and reasoning problems rather than a conventional essay-and-transcript package.

newPrograms.name: Stanford AI4ALL
newPrograms.cost: Sliding scale, free for many admitted students
newPrograms.desc: The original AI4ALL site, founded at Stanford's AI Lab to bring students underrepresented in AI into the field early. Three weeks of AI fundamentals plus a research project with a Stanford faculty mentor on applications like computational biology, robotics or NLP. Tuition is means-tested and many students attend free.
newPrograms.note: Aimed at 9th and 10th graders specifically — one of the few strong research-adjacent options for younger students.

newPrograms.name: Carleton Summer Liberal Arts Institute
newPrograms.desc: A fully funded three-week seminar for rising seniors, taught by Carleton faculty in small discussion classes across humanities, social sciences and quantitative reasoning. Students pay only travel. Designed to show what a genuine liberal-arts classroom feels like.
newPrograms.note: Free and small, which makes it competitive. A strong option for students who want humanities depth rather than another STEM camp.

newPrograms.name: Kode With Klossy
newPrograms.desc: Free two-week coding camps for girls, trans and non-binary students aged 13–18, in web development, mobile app development, machine learning and data science. Runs in cities across the US plus virtual sessions, with laptops provided where needed. Alumni get ongoing community and scholarship access.
newPrograms.note: Genuinely free, including materials. Beginner-friendly — no prior programming experience required.

newPrograms.name: Hutton Junior Fisheries Biology Program
newPrograms.desc: A paid eight-week summer mentorship in fisheries and aquatic science, matching students with a professional biologist at a state agency, university or federal lab near where they live. Field work, sampling, tagging and data collection. Comes with a $3,000 stipend.
newPrograms.note: Placements are local, so there is no housing or travel cost — one of the most accessible paid research experiences available to high schoolers.

newPrograms.name: City of Hope Roberts Summer Student Academy
newPrograms.desc: The Eugene and Ruth Roberts Summer Student Academy gives high schoolers a ten-week paid biomedical research placement at a major cancer and diabetes research centre outside Los Angeles. Students join a lab, run a project, and present at a closing symposium alongside undergraduate and graduate researchers.
newPrograms.note: Must be 16 by the program start date. Longer than most high school lab programs, which means real ownership of a project.

newPrograms.name: AwesomeMath Summer Program
newPrograms.dates: Three weeks per session, June – July 2027
newPrograms.desc: Three-week olympiad-math training sessions for students preparing for AMC, AIME, USAMO and similar competitions. Courses in number theory, combinatorics, algebra and geometry at several difficulty levels. Admission via a placement test rather than a competitive essay application.
newPrograms.note: Admission is by placement test, so it is far less of a lottery than the free olympiad programs — a good fallback if Mathcamp or PROMYS don't work out.

newPrograms.name: Barnard Pre-College Programs
newPrograms.dates: One to four weeks, June – July 2027
newPrograms.desc: Pre-college sessions for students who identify as women, on Barnard's Manhattan campus. Tracks include the four-week Liberal Arts Intensive, the Summer in the City exploration of New York institutions, and shorter STEM and writing intensives. Residential and commuter options.
newPrograms.note: Admission is rolling rather than competitive — this is a pay-to-attend enrichment program, not a selective credential.

newPrograms.name: National Student Leadership Conference
newPrograms.dates: Six to nine days, June – July 2027
newPrograms.desc: Career-exploration conferences on university campuses across the US, covering medicine, engineering, law, forensic science, international diplomacy, business and more. Simulation-heavy — mock trials, mock surgeries, mock UN sessions — rather than academic coursework. Expanding to the University of Oxford.
newPrograms.note: Open enrolment: anyone who applies and pays attends. Useful for exploring a career interest, but it carries no admissions selectivity signal.

newEvents.name: MIT THINK Scholars Program
newEvents.prize: $1,000 project budget + MIT mentorship + funded campus visit
newEvents.desc: Unlike most science competitions, THINK funds projects that have NOT been built yet. Submit a detailed proposal for a science or engineering project, and if selected you get a budget, weekly mentorship from MIT students, and a trip to campus. Ideal for students with an idea but no lab or funding.

newEvents.name: Congressional App Challenge
newEvents.prize: Winning app displayed in the US Capitol
newEvents.desc: Each participating member of Congress runs a district-level app competition, so you compete against students in your own district rather than nationally — dramatically better odds than national contests. Any platform, any language. Winners are recognised by their representative and their app is displayed in the Capitol.

newEvents.name: Coca-Cola Scholars Program
newEvents.desc: One of the largest corporate scholarship programs in the US, awarding 150 scholarships of $20,000 each to graduating seniors on the basis of leadership and service rather than test scores. Roughly 100,000 applicants a year. Opens in August of senior year and closes in October.

newEvents.name: Physics Olympiad (F=ma → USAPhO)
newEvents.prize: US Physics Team training camp + international selection
newEvents.desc: The US pathway to the International Physics Olympiad. Start with the F=ma exam in January — 25 mechanics questions in 75 minutes. Top scorers advance to USAPhO, then to the training camp at the University of Maryland, and finally five students represent the US internationally.

newEvents.name: USA Biology Olympiad (USABO)
newEvents.dl: Register through your school by Jan 2027
newEvents.prize: National Finals training camp + IBO team selection
newEvents.desc: The US selection pathway for the International Biology Olympiad, run by the same organisation behind RSI. Roughly 10,000 students take the Open Exam, 500 advance to Semifinals, and 20 reach the National Finals residential training camp. Campbell Biology is the de facto syllabus.
